{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Laurie J. Heyer''' is an American mathematician specializing in [[genomics]] and [[bioinformatics]]. She is Kimbrough Professor of Mathematics at [[Davidson College]],{{r|profile}} director of Davidson's Jay Hurt Hub for Innovation and Entrepreneurship,{{r|spotlight}} and former chair of Davidson's Mathematics and Computer Science Department.{{r|happy}}

==Education==
Heyer is a graduate of the [[University of Texas at Arlington]].{{r|profile}} She completed her Ph.D. in 1998 at the [[University of Colorado Boulder]]. Her dissertation, ''The Probabilistic Behavior of Sequence Analysis Scores with Application to Structural Alignment of RNA'', was jointly supervised by John A. Williamson and [[Gary Stormo]].{{r|mgp}}

==Textbooks==
With Malcolm Campbell, Heyer is the author of the textbook ''Discovering Genomics, Proteomics, & Bioinformatics'' (Benjamin Cummings and Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Press, 2003; 2nd ed., Pearson, 2007).{{r|dgpb}} Campbell, Heyer, and Christopher Paradise also wrote the electronic text ''Integrating Concepts in Biology''.{{r|icb}}
